title: Tuning a slow query

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Tuning a slow query

children.text: Rewriting is often better than indexing. Remove the function on the indexed column, cut the rows early, and check the plan again.
What this lesson covers
Rewrite predicates so an index can be used
Reduce the row count as early as possible
Verify the improvement with a fresh plan
This lesson sits in Query Performance, part of PostgreSQL for Developers. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Rewrite predicates so an index can be used
Reduce the row count as early as possible
Verify the improvement with a fresh plan
proTip: Wrapping an indexed column in a function usually disables the index. Transform the parameter instead.

title: Transactions and isolation levels

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Transactions and isolation levels

children.text: Isolation decides which concurrency anomalies you can still see. Read committed is the default, and it permits more than most people assume.
What this lesson covers

Compare read committed, repeatable read, and serializable
Avoid deadlocks by ordering access consistently

keyPoints: Keep transactions short and correctly scoped
Compare read committed, repeatable read, and serializable
Avoid deadlocks by ordering access consistently

title: Schema migrations without downtime

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Schema migrations without downtime

children.text: A migration runs against a live application. Expand, migrate, contract lets you change a schema while both old and new code are running.
What this lesson covers
Apply the expand, migrate, contract pattern
Avoid locks that block writes on large tables
Make every migration reversible or forward-only on purpose
This lesson sits in Operating Postgres, part of PostgreSQL for Developers. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Apply the expand, migrate, contract pattern
Avoid locks that block writes on large tables
Make every migration reversible or forward-only on purpose

title: Backups and connection pooling

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Backups and connection pooling

children.text: A backup you have never restored is a hypothesis. A pooler is what stops a few hundred idle app connections from exhausting the server.
What this lesson covers
Take backups and rehearse a restore
Understand point-in-time recovery
Pool connections in front of the database
This lesson sits in Operating Postgres, part of PostgreSQL for Developers. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Take backups and rehearse a restore
Understand point-in-time recovery
Pool connections in front of the database
proTip: An untested backup is not a backup. Restore one on a schedule.

title: Images, containers, and Dockerfiles

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Images, containers, and Dockerfiles

children.text: An image is a stacked filesystem plus metadata; a container is a running instance of one. Every Dockerfile instruction is a layer.
What this lesson covers
Distinguish an image from a running container
Write a Dockerfile that builds reproducibly
Choose a base image deliberately
This lesson sits in Containers and Images, part of DevOps with Docker and Kubernetes. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

Write a Dockerfile that builds reproducibly

title: Layers, caching, and multi-stage builds

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Layers, caching, and multi-stage builds

children.text: Instruction order decides your build time. Copy dependency manifests before source, and use a multi-stage build to leave the toolchain behind.
What this lesson covers
Order instructions so the cache survives code changes
Separate build and runtime with multi-stage builds
Cut image size and shrink the attack surface
This lesson sits in Containers and Images, part of DevOps with Docker and Kubernetes. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Order instructions so the cache survives code changes
Separate build and runtime with multi-stage builds
Cut image size and shrink the attack surface
proTip: Copy your lockfile and install dependencies before copying source. Otherwise every edit invalidates the install layer.
